- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% to counteract pessimism.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model often overreacts and forecasts a prolonged overshoot; reduce forecast by 3–5% in next 5–7 days to avoid overcorrection.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.7) and price is trending up, model frequently overestimates near-term gains; cap forecast at 10–15% above recent high to avoid volatility overfitting.
- When sentiment oscillates between 0.2–0.5, model shows persistent lag in price reversal; add 1–2 days of lagged price adjustment to forecast to align with sentiment shifts.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (price drops after 3+ consecutive days above 65), model often fails to recognize it; apply a 2–3 day mean-reversion buffer in forecast to avoid overbought bias.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates true price by 2–4% when sentiment is neutral or slightly negative; add 1–2% to forecast to compensate for sentiment-induced downward bias.
